hints: Write `http://` and `https://` one above the other and find the first character where they differ. To tell them apart, the check has to look at least that far.
The likely mistake is treating "starts with http" as "is HTTPS". A plain http:// address starts with those same letters, so the check can't tell the two apart.
solution_explanation: Only the `https://` scheme means the connection is protected by TLS. Checking for the full `https://` prefix rejects plain `http://` addresses, which slipped through when the check looked for "http" alone.
